name: Cabinet
description: A lightweight self-hosted file cabinet and document manager.
summary: Cabinet v0.5.0 (2026-07-04) is a major release with 238 commits, introducing Connect Knowledge for integrating cloud drives (Google Drive, iCloud, OneDrive, Dropbox) into rooms, a significantly expanded Integrations Hub with 52 connectors (Slack, Google, Microsoft 365, Snowflake, LinkedIn, Discord, Telegram), agent Channels, and a Telegram remote-control gateway. Auth improvements include PBKDF2 password hashing with per-install salt and login rate-limiting. v0.6.0 introduces a self-update mechanism, with future releases published at https://github.com/cabinetai/cabinet-releases.

answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes, v0.5.0 released 2026-07-04 with 238 commits and v0.6.0 followed shortly after
answers.Does it support user authentication?: Yes, PBKDF2 password hashing with per-install salt, login rate-limiting, and KB_PASSWORD gate for daemon

breaking_excerpts: Clean-path routing: the app serves clean URLs instead of hash routes across web and Electron; old hash links resolve via a marker-scan parser but canonical form is now path-based.
Channels on-disk rename: the internal team-chat directory moved from '.slack' to '.channels', scoped per room.
v0.6.0 moves the update mechanism to a new updater; future releases are published at https://github.com/cabinetai/cabinet-releases instead of the original repository.

alternatives.name: Paperless-ngx
alternatives.review: Paperless-ngx offers far more advanced OCR, tagging, and document indexing than Cabinet, but comes with a heavier setup and resource footprint.

alternatives.name: Teedy
alternatives.review: Teedy provides a more full-featured document management system with workflows and metadata, but is heavier and more complex to self-host than Cabinet.

alternatives.name: Docspell
alternatives.review: Docspell excels at automated document processing and tagging but requires more infrastructure setup compared to Cabinet's lightweight approach.

alternatives.name: Nextcloud
alternatives.review: Nextcloud is a much broader platform covering file storage, collaboration, and more, making it feature-rich but significantly heavier than Cabinet.

alternatives.name: Filestash
alternatives.review: Filestash is similarly lightweight and self-hosted but focuses more on being a universal file browser across storage backends rather than document management.
